item.title: Senate moves to recouple D.C. tax policy
item.description: The Senate voted to disallow Washington D.C.'s attempt to decouple its tax policy from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, as the city's mayor charts more budget challenges in the near future.

item.title: Munis firmer, sizable inflows continue
item.description: Currently, munis are largely operating "in their own world" — ignoring rich valuations and upcoming supply, said Kim Olsan, senior fixed income portfolio manager at NewSquare Capital, in a report.

item.title: California counties ask voters for sales taxes to backfill Medicaid cuts
item.description: Los Angeles County and Contra Costa County supervisors both approved placing sales tax measures on the June ballot to address federal Medicaid cuts.

item.title: As shutdown nears, FEMA warns of delayed disaster response
item.description: The agency's Disaster Recovery Fund has a sufficient balance for the near term but a funding lapse will translate into longer response times to local and state governments, FEMA's associate administrator warned.

item.title: Austin bond-related cases seek Texas high court rulings
item.description: Cases involving bonds for the city's convention center and a light-rail project are pending before the Texas Supreme Court.

item.title: California sees healthy demand for water system revenue bonds
item.description: A California Department of Water Resources issuance, based on a resolution extending contracts with water agency customers, drew strong demand.

item.title: Capital spending may increase due to rising needs: Analyst
item.description: Bonding should increase in the next few years to address aged state and local infrastructure, Moody's Vice President Dan Seymour said.

item.title: Dallas sued by Texas attorney general over police funding
item.description: The lawsuit contends the city is not complying with a 2024 voter-approved charter amendment requiring increased spending on police.

item.title: Bond yields fall after CPI report shows tamer inflation
item.description: "Unsurprisingly, the market is taking these numbers in stride, with the bond market only slightly higher after a large rally over the last couple of days due to the equity market sell-off," said John Kerschner, global head of securitized products and portfolio manager at Janus Henderson Investors.

item.title: Central Alabama Water downgraded by S&P
item.description: The rating agency, which also put the bonds on CreditWatch Negative, cited weakening liquidity and aging assets.
